title: Check the negatives around a quoted line
statement: When narration paraphrases or embeds a quoted line, check that its negatives still say what the line says, since a carried-over negative can make a double negative that reverses it.
detail: A quality pass on a Grade 9 unit's knowledge base found guide narration that kept a quoted line's 'cannot' beside a 'not' of its own, a double negative that reversed what the line says (`g9/sources/1. Act 1 - Knowledge Base - Overview.csv`, line 144). The line itself already carries two negatives (`g9/sources/Act 1 reading texts/Act 1/1. 1.1 - Iago_s Introduction - Text.docx`, lines 68-69). The narration was reworded to a positive form and the case marked fixed.

evidence.quote: originally said ""not all masters 'cannot be truly followed'"", a double negative that reverses the line. Changed to ""not all masters can be 'truly followed.'"" Fixed.

evidence.path: sources/Act 1 reading texts/Act 1/1. 1.1 - Iago_s Introduction - Text.docx
evidence.quote: We cannot all be masters, nor all masters Cannot be truly followed.
